section: Environmental Studies · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching EVS
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: A teacher asks pupils to observe a burning candle, form a guess about why the flame changes colour, and then test that guess with a simple experiment. This approach chiefly develops:

options.option_text: Scientific temper and process skills of observation, hypothesis and experimentation
Rote memorisation of facts about candles

explanation: This inquiry-based sequence builds scientific temper and process skills, the central aim of EVS/science teaching under NCF 2005, rather than mere fact recall.

section: Environmental Studies · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching EVS
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: At the primary level, EVS is typically taught as an integrated subject combining elements of science and social studies, mainly because:

options.option_text: Young children experience their environment holistically, not in separate subject silos
It reduces the number of textbooks a school needs to print
Science and social studies have no genuine connection at any level
It allows the school to skip teaching science altogether

explanation: NCF-informed pedagogy integrates natural and social environment themes at the primary stage because young children encounter their surroundings as a connected whole, not as isolated academic disciplines.

section: Environmental Studies · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching EVS
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: Taking pupils on a short walk around the school to observe local plants, insects and soil types is an example of the:
explanation: Direct observation of the immediate environment builds first-hand understanding of EVS concepts, consistent with activity-based, learner-centred pedagogy.
